summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with a custom interactive code-search tool called `rgf` that combines ripgrep, fzf, and bat. It installs the necessary command-line tools, writes a zsh function that lets you search code and open results in VSCode at the exact line number, configures zsh to autoload this function, and finally creates a demo project with various code patterns (secrets, TODOs, etc.) to search through.

explanations.3: This tells the package installer to run in non-interactive mode so it won't prompt you during the Docker build — it just installs everything automatically.
explanations.7: Ubuntu's default package repositories only include 'main' and 'restricted' packages, but fzf and bat are in 'universe' and 'multiverse', so this line adds those repositories so apt can find those tools.
explanations.15: After installing packages, we delete the apt cache to make the Docker image smaller — those cached files aren't needed once installation is done.
explanations.20: We're creating the directory structure where the custom zsh function will live (zsh functions are typically stored in `~/.zsh/fns/`).
explanations.22: This uses `printf` with multiple lines to write out the entire `rgf` function as text — each `'...'` string becomes one line in the final file.
explanations.32: This detects whether we're on macOS (Darwin), Linux, or another OS so we can suggest the right install command if dependencies are missing.
explanations.44: Ubuntu/Debian packages the `bat` tool as `batcat` instead of `bat`, so we check for both names to see which one is available.
explanations.72: We're creating a variable to store the correct command name for bat — either `bat` or `batcat` depending on which one exists.
explanations.83: We create a temporary file because piping directly to fzf in some shells (like WSL subshells) can freeze the interactive UI; writing to a file avoids that problem.
explanations.96: We read the contents of the temp file into a variable — the `<` redirects the file's contents into the variable.
explanations.104: We strip out ANSI color codes (the escape sequences that add colors) from the selected line, then use `cut` to extract just the filename (the part before the first colon).
explanations.115: The `>` redirects all the printf output to write the file `/root/.zsh/fns/rgf` with the function code.
explanations.120: The `>>` appends these two lines to `.zshrc` (as opposed to `>` which would overwrite) so zsh loads and enables the rgf function automatically on startup.
explanations.126: We're creating demo files with realistic code-search scenarios — a `.env` file with a secret, files with TODO/FIXME/HACK comments, a hardcoded port in compose.yml, and a TypeScript interface.
explanations.141: This customizes the shell prompt to show a whale emoji and cyan username so you can clearly see when you're inside this container versus your host machine.
explanations.143: This sets the default command to run when the container starts — an interactive login shell so you can type commands right away.
